editorial.headline: The Business of Video on Demand
editorial.standfirst: A clear route for on-demand video services nationally, with Bali remaining outside the island-wide PMA moratorium block but subject to address-level verification.
editorial.body:
On-demand video distribution and streaming is the activity at the centre of this code: the operation of services that deliver video when viewers choose to watch it. Its scope includes programming video-on-demand channels, distributing such video through subscription or advertising models, and enabling downloads of digital video content. That content may belong to a third party or be original material produced by the operator. It also includes game-video streaming where the audience watches rather than plays.

The activity is open across the full business-scale range stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the definition is built around the service of distributing and streaming video, rather than a single commercial format. A business may operate an on-demand channel, distribute subscription video, offer advertising-supported viewing, make digital video available for download, or stream gameplay for viewing only. The common thread is the delivery of video content on demand.

Nationally, this is an open activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In practical terms, the record does not place the foreign stake below full ownership at the national level. The national position is therefore straightforward: the activity is TERBUKA, and its stated ceiling permits 100% foreign ownership. That clarity should not obscure the commercial breadth of the code, which can encompass both third-party content and content produced by the operator itself.

Bali presents a distinct but not prohibitive picture. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island on a permanent basis. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: the Bali record places it in an OK-or-higher-risk position and states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. The remaining qualification is specific and limited: the position should be verified for the relevant address. For a PMA applicant considering Bali, the accurate conclusion is neither a blanket refusal nor an invented guarantee; it is an activity that remains outside the moratorium block, with address-level verification still called for.
